findings.detail: No ADR covering the BindingRepository extraction was found in docs/adr/. Searched for 'BindingRepository', 'binding_repository', 'repository unit-of-work', 'unit of work', 'no-journal', 'no journal', 'format-migration', 'format migration', 'selective publication', 'rollback', 'partial-state', 'ordered partial', 'recovery boundary', 'exact-match recovery', 'extraction', '5142', 'rp02' — all returned no matches. The existing ADR 0027 (docs/adr/0027-reconciler-binding-lifecycle.md) covers binding lifecycle identity rules but does not address: the BindingRepository extraction, repository unit-of-work durability vs. tickets publication, ordered partial-state behavior (rotation-before-live ordering), selective publication seam, rollback of the facade delegation, or the no-journal/no-format-migration decision. No other ADR in the directory covers these topics.
findings.remediation: Add a new ADR (e.g. docs/adr/NNNN-reconciler-binding-repository.md) that explicitly covers: (1) BindingRepository as sole owner of the four state paths, (2) ordered partial-state behavior (rotation written before live replacement), (3) selective publication seam (five bridge-state files only), (4) rollback procedure (reverting facade delegation restores previous implementation), and (5) the no-journal/no-format-migration decision.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
